name: MITRE ATT&CK
description: MITRE ATT&CK is a globally-accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques based on real-world observations. It is organized as matrices (Enterprise, Mobile, ICS) of Tactics (the why — e.g., Initial Access, Execution, Persistence) crossed with Techniques (the how — e.g., Phishing, Command and Scripting Interpreter). Each Technique has sub-techniques, mitigations, detections, references to known threat groups, and software used. ATT&CK is the de facto common language for adversary behavior in threat intelligence, detection engineering, and red/purple-team work. The Enterprise matrix covers Windows, macOS, Linux, Containers, Cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP/SaaS/IaaS/Office 365), and Network platforms.
relationToCloudSecurity: ATT&CK Enterprise includes dedicated Cloud platform coverage (IaaS/SaaS/Office 365/Azure AD/Google Workspace) with cloud-specific techniques and sub-techniques. Cloud security tools commonly map detections and alerts to ATT&CK technique IDs. ATT&CK is the substrate that CSA's threat-modeling work, MITRE D3FEND, and the Center for Threat-Informed Defense build on.
relationToAISecurity: ATT&CK addresses traditional adversary behavior; AI-specific adversary techniques (model evasion, training-data poisoning, prompt injection, etc.) are covered by MITRE ATLAS, which uses an ATT&CK-style structure but is a separate matrix.

license.notes: Corrected 2026-08-12: this entry previously stated that mitre/cti is 'published under Apache-2.0 for code'. That is wrong. Both mitre/cti and mitre-attack/attack-stix-data ship a LICENSE.txt containing the MITRE ATT&CK license (non-exclusive, royalty-free, for research/development/commercial use), NOT Apache-2.0 — GitHub's license detector reports NOASSERTION for both. Redistribution requires reproducing MITRE's copyright designation verbatim: '(c) 2026 The MITRE Corporation. This work is reproduced and distributed with the permission of The MITRE Corporation.' Note that mitre-attack/attack-navigator (a separate tool repo) IS Apache-2.0 — that may be the source of the original confusion.

lifecycle.notes: Roughly twice-yearly majors plus patch releases. Current upstream is v19.2 (2026-08-05) for all three matrices; index.json lists 41 Enterprise releases. Two parallel repos are both current and were tagged v19.2 within minutes of each other: mitre-attack/attack-stix-data is STIX 2.1 (canonical, prefer for new work) and mitre/cti is STIX 2.0 (legacy serialization, still maintained, also carries the CAPEC STIX distribution). The difference is serialization format, not content.

current_extraction.notes: ATT&CK is published as STIX 2.0/2.1 bundles at https://github.com/mitre-attack/attack-stix-data (Apache-2.0, ~50MB per matrix). This repo references it rather than mirroring — the upstream is authoritative and version-tagged. Consumers should pull from upstream by tag/release. Enterprise/Mobile/ICS matrices each have their own JSON bundles.

extraction_history.reason: README pointer to upstream cti repo
Confirmed reference-only model — STIX bundles are large (~50MB each) and version-tagged in upstream GitHub repo, no value in mirroring

scope.license: MITRE ATT&CK license (attribution required) for both data repos
scope.release_pattern: Git tags / GitHub Releases on both repos; attack-stix-data uses vN.N, mitre/cti uses ATT&CK-vN.N
scope.identifier_pattern: IDs appear as external_references[].external_id where source_name starts with 'mitre'. Verified prefixes in the v19.2 ICS bundle: TA#### (tactic), T####[.###] (technique/sub-technique), S#### (software), G#### (group), C#### (campaign), M#### (mitigation), DS#### (data source), A#### (asset, ICS), and AN####/DET####/DC#### (detection strategies, detections, analytic components - object types introduced in v18, so pre-v18 consumers will not recognize them).
scope.deprecation_mechanism: Present, unlike ATLAS. Objects carry revoked and x_mitre_deprecated flags plus revoked-by relationships, so retired IDs can be followed forward programmatically. The v19.2 ICS bundle alone contains 11 revoked objects, 37 deprecated, and 11 revoked-by relationships.

notes: ATT&CK is the most-cited adversary behavior framework in the industry. Downstream consumers should pin to specific ATT&CK versions for reproducibility — technique IDs are comparatively stable and retirements are traceable via revoked-by, but coverage grows release-over-release and new object types appear between majors.
